channel.title: SecuBuzz · Cybersecurity News Briefs
channel.description: Fast, factual 60-word cybersecurity briefs and CISA KEV alerts for security professionals.

item.title: Microsoft Tests Fix for Windows 11 Bluetooth Audio Drops
item.description: Microsoft is testing a fix for a long-standing Windows 11 Bluetooth audio quality drop affecting headphone users. The issue stems from an audio driver mis-handling of Bluetooth codec parameters, causing significant degradation but lacking remote code execution or data exfiltration. Microsoft has released a test build; users should install the forthcoming update once available to restore audio fidelity.

item.title: iTerm2 Remote Code Execution Flaw Lets Hackers Run Malicious Commands by Displaying Crafted Files
item.description: A security flaw in iTerm2, a macOS terminal emulator, lets attackers run commands when a user displays a specially crafted file in a vulnerable terminal session. The user does not have to run the file as a script or paste a command supplied by the attacker.

item.title: FBI Investigates National Crime Information Center Breach
item.description: A breach of the FBI’s National Crime Information Center has been reported, prompting an investigation by the agency. The incident potentially exposes sensitive criminal records and investigative data, though the extent of compromised information remains unverified. FBI officials advise affected stakeholders to monitor for unauthorized disclosures and to implement enhanced monitoring of internal access controls.

item.title: CrowdStrike Agrees to Acquire Zscaler for $43.9B
item.description: CrowdStrike announced an all-stock acquisition of Zscaler valued at approximately $43.9 billion, creating a combined cloud-security entity. The deal grants each Zscaler share 1.135 CrowdStrike shares, implying a premium of roughly 34 % over Zscaler’s closing price. Post-closing, CrowdStrike shareholders will own about 84.1 % of the merged publicly company, pending regulatory approvals.

item.title: ScreenConnect CVE-2026-84869 Enables MSP Technician Hijack
item.description: Threat actors exploited a patched flaw in ConnectWise ScreenConnect, identified as CVE-2026-84869, to hijack managed service provider technician workstations. The CVSS 9.9 score marks it as a critical unauthenticated RCE that lets a guest transfer and execute malicious payloads. ConnectWise issued an emergency patch; administrators must apply it immediately and limit guest access to prevent exploitation.

item.title: N-Able Exposes CVE-2026-134624 SSRF in Mail Assure
item.description: N-Able disclosed a critical SSRF flaw, CVE-2026-134624, discovered during an investigation of its Mail Assure and SpamExperts Hosted Cloud breach. The vulnerability permits a high-privilege API user to open connections to arbitrary internal systems, enabling potential lateral movement. N-Able recommends applying the vendor patch immediately and restricting API access to mitigate exploitation risks.

item.title: Red Hat Issues libXrender Security Update
item.description: Red Hat released an important security update for libXrender on RHEL 7 Extended Lifecycle Support. The update addresses one or more vulnerabilities with CVSS scores available via linked CVE references, though specific IDs are not listed. Apply the libXrender update immediately, promptly, and follow Red Hat advisories for installation guidance.

item.title: Red Hat Issues librabbitmq Security Update
item.description: Red Hat released an important security update for librabbitmq on RHEL 10. The update mitigates vulnerabilities with CVSS scores available via linked CVE references, though specific IDs are not listed, and it applies to all affected librabbitmq packages. Install the librabbitmq update promptly and consult Red Hat advisories for detailed guidance.

item.title: Red Hat Releases libXrender Security Update
item.description: Red Hat released a security update for libXrender on Enterprise Linux 8.8, addressing multiple vulnerabilities rated as Important. The update includes patches for CVEs referenced in the advisory, each with a CVSS base score that informs the severity. Administrators should apply the update promptly and verify that libXrender is at the latest patched version to maintain system integrity.

item.title: RHSA-2026:102288: Important: Red Hat AMQ Broker 7.14.2 release and security update
item.description: Red Hat AMQ Broker 7.14.2 is now available from the Red Hat Customer Portal. Red Hat Product Security has rated this update as having a security impact of Important. A Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) base score, which gives a detailed severity rating, is available for each vulnerability from the CVE link(s) in the References section.

item.title: Peruvian Call Center Operator Sentenced to Eight Years
item.description: A Peruvian call-center operator received an eight-year sentence for facilitating a government-impersonation fraud that targeted over 30,000 Spanish-speaking U.S. residents. The scheme used deceptive calls to coerce victims into revealing personal data, leading to millions of dollars stolen. The conviction highlights the legal consequences for individuals aiding such fraud operations.

item.title: Cisco Expressway CVE-2026-76466 Enables Root Access
item.description: Attackers are exploiting Cisco Expressway’s critical flaw, CVE-2026-76466, to gain root access and infiltrate internal networks. The vulnerability, confirmed by F6 researchers, allows unauthenticated remote code execution with a public PoC, posing a severe enterprise risk. Cisco has issued a patch; administrators must apply it immediately and verify device integrity to prevent exploitation.

item.title: Essay Argues AI Lacks Legal Rights
item.description: Character.AI petitioned a court to dismiss a death suit, claiming chatbot’s speech was protected and the company was a service, not a product. Judge Anne Conway rejected both arguments in May 2025, holding that the chatbot’s content could be subject to product-liability law. The ruling underscores the debate over AI accountability and limits of First Amendment protections for machine-generated speech.

item.title: BadBox 3.0 Ad Fraud Operation Disrupted
item.description: Backdoors on low-cost consumer devices enabled the BadBox 3.0 ad-fraud operation, delivering modules that generated 40 billion bid requests daily. The operation leveraged residential-proxy capabilities to obfuscate traffic, creating an ad-fraud network that inflated auction volumes and siphoned revenue from publishers. Security teams coordinated a takedown that disrupted the backdoor infrastructure, halting bid-request generation and exposing compromised devices for remediation.

item.title: CrowdStrike to Acquire Zscaler for $43.9B
item.description: CrowdStrike announced a $43.9 billion acquisition of Zscaler, aiming to combine their security platforms and generate over $10 billion in annual recurring revenue. The deal positions CrowdStrike as a leading provider of integrated cloud-native security services, expanding its market reach across identity, network, and application layers.

item.title: Red Hat Issues Low-Impact edk2 Update
item.description: Red Hat released a low-impact update for the edk2 firmware component on RHEL 8.4 Advanced Mission Critical Update Support and Extended Update Support Long-Life Add-On. The update addresses multiple security issues, each with a CVSS base score listed in the CVE references, but no active exploitation has been reported. Red Hat recommends applying the update immediately to maintain system integrity.

item.title: RHSA-2026:102253: Important: kernel security, bug fix, and enhancement update
item.description: An update for kernel is now available for Red Hat Enterprise Linux 10. Red Hat Product Security has rated this update as having a security impact of Important. A Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) base score, which gives a detailed severity rating, is available for each vulnerability from the CVE link(s) in the References section.

item.title: Cairn Framework Used to Exploit Medical AI Zero-Day
item.description: A Chinese-nexus threat actor used the open-source Cairn framework to exploit a zero-day in a medical imaging AI application. The zero-day enabled remote code execution after initial failed attempts, giving the attacker a foothold without a disclosed CVE. No vendor patch exists; teams should monitor exploitation, harden AI applications, and limit autonomous framework use.

item.title: GL.iNet Cloud Flaw Enables Malware on Routers
item.description: A flaw in GL.iNet’s cloud remote-management service granted attackers unauthorized access to routers and KVM devices, allowing malware and backdoor installation. The vulnerability, discovered on November 20 2026, was patched by GL.iNet, but affected devices still need a firmware update to eliminate the risk. Security teams should verify firmware versions and apply the latest update; no additional workarounds are documented.

item.title: Attackers exploited Microsoft Entra Connect Health flaw to access tenant data
item.description: Attackers exploited a vulnerability in the Microsoft Entra Connect Health API to read the technical contact email addresses and configuration details of Entra tenants, the company warned affected organizations. Microsoft Entra Connect Health is a cloud-based monitoring service that gives administrators a single view of the health, performance and alerts for their on-premises identity infrastructure in the Microsoft Entra admin center.

item.title: AI-Driven Breach Exposes Over 1 Million Records
item.description: Chinese-speaking hackers leveraged an AI testing tool to autonomously breach ten organizations between August and September 2026, exposing over one million personal records from a single victim. The tool performed most attack steps, with operators only specifying targets, indicating a low-effort exploitation chain. Affected entities should conduct forensic investigations, strengthen access controls, and notify impacted individuals per regulatory requirements.

item.title: Critical ASP.NET AntiCsrf Flaw Enables Remote Code Execution Without Authentication
item.description: A critical flaw in the Idunno.AntiCsrf library used by legacy ASP.NET WebForms apps has been actively exploited, letting attackers run arbitrary code on servers without authentication. The vulnerability, CVE-2026-131914, scores 9.3 on CVSS and has already caused incidents worldwide. Affected organizations must update or remove the library immediately and apply vendor patches to mitigate the risk.

item.title: Red Hat releases webkit2gtk3 security update
item.description: Red Hat released a critical webkit2gtk3 security update for RHEL 8.4 Advanced Mission Critical and Extended Update Support. The update fixes multiple vulnerabilities, each with a CVSS base score in the CVE references, and is rated Important. Apply the update promptly today to prevent exploitation of the affected webkit2gtk3 components.

item.title: Red Hat Issues Critical PHP 8.3 Security Update
item.description: Red Hat released a critical security update for the php:8.3 module on RHEL 9, addressing multiple vulnerabilities. The update is rated Critical, with CVSS base scores provided for each vulnerability via the referenced CVE links, indicating high-severity flaws. Apply the patch promptly; no workarounds are available, and the update should be deployed across all affected systems.

item.title: Red Hat Releases Kernel Security Update for RHEL 8.6
item.description: Red Hat issued a kernel security update for RHEL 8.6 Advanced Mission Critical Update Support and Extended Update Support Long-Life Add-On, addressing multiple vulnerabilities. The update carries an Important impact rating, with CVSS base scores available for each vulnerability via the referenced CVE links. Security teams should apply the patch immediately to mitigate potential exploitation; no workarounds are currently recommended.

item.title: Microsoft Confirms Printing Issues on Forcepoint Systems
item.description: Microsoft confirmed that the KB5132043 Windows 11 hotpatch caused printing failures on systems running Forcepoint DLP software. The issue does not represent a security vulnerability but disrupts print functionality for affected users. Microsoft advises users to postpone the hotpatch until a fix is released or to revert to a previous Windows 11 build.

item.title: GL.iNet Cloud flaw exploited for malware
item.description: Hackers exploited a flaw in GL.iNet's GoodCloud remote-management service to install malware on customer routers and KVM devices. The vulnerability allowed remote code execution via authenticated access, and the attacker leveraged it to deploy malicious binaries before the company patched the flaw. GL.iNet has blocked the attack vector and recommends users apply the firmware update immediately to prevent further infections.

item.title: Signal Blocks AI Assistants From Accessing Private Messages
item.description: Signal updated its app to block AI assistants on iOS 27 and Android, preventing them from capturing users’ private message content. The change stops assistants like Siri and Google Gemini from reading the screen to answer queries, protecting data stores. No vulnerability is reported; the update is a privacy safeguard that requires installing the latest Signal version.

item.title: Samsung Securities Breach Exposes 8,241 Customers' Data
item.description: Samsung Securities reported a breach exposing personal data of 8,241 customers after unauthorized access to its Voice of Customer (VOC) website. The breach involved credential theft and internal compromise, but impact was limited to the VOC system. Samsung Securities advised affected customers to monitor accounts, change passwords, and is investigating while notifying regulators.

item.title: AI-Assisted Attacks Trigger Unauthorized Bank Transfers
item.description: AI-assisted threat actors targeted Indian ICT assets, forcing unauthorized financial transfers at banks and fintech firms. The attacks leveraged machine-learning-driven phishing and credential-stealing techniques, exploiting known login-bypass flaws to move laterally within banking networks. Red CERT-In urges immediate patching of vulnerable systems and enhanced monitoring of transaction logs to detect further unauthorized activity.

item.title: BADBOX 3.0 TV Boxes Generate 40 Billion Ad Requests
item.description: BADBOX 3.0 infected low-cost TV boxes produced roughly 40 billion ad bid requests daily, exceeding 4% of all connected TV traffic. The malware hijacked ad rendering processes, enabling stealthy traffic injection without user awareness and creating a large-scale advertising fraud network.

item.title: Bulgarian Government Breach Exposes 62 Million Pages
item.description: Hackers accessed Bulgarian state administration networks for five years, exfiltrating 130 GB of documents. The intrusion leveraged covert persistence mechanisms to download over 62 million pages, representing a significant compromise of sensitive government data. Bulgarian authorities disrupted the operation and are investigating the breach; no vendor patch is applicable, but organizations should review network segmentation and intrusion detection controls.

item.title: Weekly Security Roundup: Nov 16-22
item.description: Malwarebytes Labs released a weekly security roundup covering topics from Nov 16 to Nov 22, 2026. The report summarizes emerging threats, vulnerability disclosures, and defensive recommendations observed during that period, including zero-day exploits and supply-chain risks. The summary is available for security teams to review trends, update defenses, and threat intelligence.

item.title: Red Hat Kernel Update for RHEL 10.0 EUS
item.description: Red Hat released a kernel update for Enterprise Linux 10.0 Extended Update Support, addressing multiple security issues. The advisory notes an Important security impact, with CVSS base scores linked to each vulnerability, indicating potential high-severity flaws. Security teams should apply the update immediately to mitigate the identified kernel vulnerabilities, as no workarounds are provided.

item.title: Cisco Expressway Zero-Day Exploit Enables Remote Code Execution
item.description: A zero-day vulnerability (CVE-2026-76466) in Cisco Expressway gateways has been exploited by attackers to breach internal networks. The unauthenticated remote flaw permits arbitrary code execution, and it has been confirmed as a critical CVSS-rated zero-day used in the wild. Cisco has released a patch; organizations must apply it immediately and verify CISA’s Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog for guidance.

item.title: Malicious Ad Domains Steal iPhone Crypto Recovery Phrases
item.description: Hackers leveraged over 480 malicious ad domains to compromise iPhones and exfiltrate crypto wallet recovery phrases, passwords, and personal data. The MoldyRoost operation exploited ad rendering engine flaws, enabling credential theft without user interaction across 47+ countries. Apple issued a security advisory urging iOS updates and users to avoid suspicious ads; security teams should monitor ad traffic and enforce sandboxing.

item.title: Red Hat Kernel Update for RHEL 8
item.description: Red Hat issued a kernel update for Enterprise Linux 8, addressing several security issues. The advisory labels the update as Important, with CVSS base scores linked to each vulnerability, implying high-severity flaws. Apply the update promptly to remediate the kernel vulnerabilities; no workarounds are provided, and ensure system integrity today.

item.title: Red Hat Kernel-rt Update for RHEL 8
item.description: Red Hat released a kernel-rt update for Enterprise Linux 8, fixing multiple security defects. The advisory rates the update as Important, with CVSS base scores linked to each vulnerability, indicating high-severity flaws. Security teams should apply the kernel-rt patch immediately; no workarounds exist, and system stability must be verified today.

item.title: Cancer Institute Tackles Shadow IT in Research
item.description: Istituto Nazionale Tumori (INT) discusses how to keep a cancer research hospital operational while protecting against cyberattacks. The director explains collaboration with partner hospitals in the Rare Cancer Network, challenges when staff cannot access chemotherapy plans, and why banning shadow IT rarely fixes gaps. INT also highlights the most burdensome EU regulation and outlines its approach to secure research workflows.

item.title: Xalgorix Introduces AI-Powered Pen Testing Tool
item.description: Xalgorix, an open-source AI penetration testing framework, validates findings through a dual-agent verification process. The primary agent identifies potential bugs, while a secondary agent attempts to exploit them; failures to confirm a bug result in a flagged finding for manual review, reducing false positives. The tool is available for community use and encourages reviewers to assess flagged vulnerabilities before reporting.

item.title: Early Black Friday Scams Emerge Without Red Flags
item.description: Scammers began posting fake Black Friday deals on September 1, earlier than last year, rarely referencing the holiday or using familiar domain names. The campaigns appear as Facebook group posts or Google Sites pages, mimicking retailer sale language promoting software, payment, travel, or crypto offers. Security teams should monitor social media and verify vendor legitimacy before engaging with such promotions.

item.title: Red Hat Issues Cockpit Security Patch
item.description: Red Hat released a security update for the Cockpit management interface on Enterprise Linux 10.0 Extended Update Support. The advisory references multiple CVEs with CVSS base scores, but no active exploitation is reported, and the update is classified as Important by Product Security. Administrators should apply the Cockpit patch promptly to address the identified vulnerabilities.

item.title: Red Hat Releases Kernel Security Update
item.description: Red Hat issued a kernel update for Enterprise Linux 9 addressing multiple security bugs. The advisory lists several CVEs with CVSS base scores, but no active exploitation is reported, and the update is rated as Important by Product Security. Users should apply the kernel patch immediately to mitigate the identified vulnerabilities.

item.title: ISACA Updates COBIT 7 with AI Risk Scenarios
item.description: ISACA released COBIT 7, the latest version of its governance framework, adding AI risk scenarios. The update provides comprehensive guidance, a digital platform, and customizable resources to help organizations manage emerging AI risks. Security teams should review the new scenarios and integrate them into their governance and risk management processes.

item.title: Red Hat Releases MySQL 8.4 Security Update
item.description: Red Hat issued a security update for the mysql:8.4 module on Red Enterprise Linux 9.8 Extended Update Support. The update addresses multiple vulnerabilities, each with a CVSS base score listed in the CVE references, but no active exploitation has been reported. Administrators should apply the RHSA-2026:102188 update promptly to mitigate potential exploitation of the identified flaws.

item.title: Red Hat Releases Important Git-LFS Security Update
item.description: Red Hat issued an important security update for git-lfs on RHEL 9.8 Extended Update Support. The advisory indicates that the update addresses one or more vulnerabilities, each with a CVSS base score available via the referenced CVE links. Users should apply the git-lfs update immediately to mitigate the identified security risks.

item.title: Red Hat Issues Moderate OpenSSH Security Update
item.description: Red Hat released a moderate security update for OpenSSH on RHEL 9, addressing weaknesses that could allow remote attackers to gain elevated privileges. The advisory references multiple CVEs, each with a CVSS base score provided, indicating the severity of the flaws. Administrators should apply the OpenSSH update promptly to mitigate the disclosed vulnerabilities and prevent privilege escalation.

item.title: Red Hat Releases Kernel Update for RHEL 10
item.description: Red Hat released a kernel update for Red Enterprise Linux 10 to address multiple security bugs. The update contains fixes for several kernel vulnerabilities, each with a CVSS base score listed in the CVE references, but no active exploitation has been reported. Administrators should apply the RHSA-2026:102168 update promptly to mitigate potential exploitation of the identified flaws.

item.title: Flatpak Update Addresses Important Security Flaw
item.description: Red Hat released a security update for Flatpak on Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9, addressing an important vulnerability in the container runtime. The advisory notes the flaw’s importance but does not list a CVE identifier; CVSS base scores are provided in the references. Apply the Flatpak update promptly; no further mitigations are required.

item.title: Thunderbird Update Fixes Important Security Flaw
item.description: A security update for Thunderbird on Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9.8 EUS addresses an important vulnerability affecting the email client. The flaw, rated Important by Red Hat Product Security, lacks a publicly disclosed CVE identifier but is documented with CVSS base scores in the advisory references. Red Hat recommends applying the update immediately; no additional workarounds are specified.
